title: Felix and the Safehouse
premise: Xanthe Reyes, a freelance interpreter who quietly handles the peace delegation's dirty work—discreet translations, deniable messages, cases no one wants on record—is approached by Felix, a stranger who claims she once saved his life, a favor she has no memory of. He offers her a debt repaid: intelligence that a catastrophic attack is scheduled during the delegation's final summit, engineered to look like an accident and bury the peace process forever. As Xanthe and Felix trace the plot through the delegation's own ranks, she discovers the conspiracy implicates the handler who made her career—and that staying invisible means letting it happen. In the end, Xanthe sacrifices her anonymity and nearly her life to expose the attack, choosing justice outside the law and a fragile, hard-won love over the safe, unseen existence she built.
about_author: Freya Dunmore is a former conference interpreter who spent a decade working behind the glass of international negotiations before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about the people history forgets to name, drawing on the moral gray zones she witnessed firsthand.

chapters.title: The Glass Booth
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. During a fractious pre-summit session in Geneva, Xanthe interprets not just words but intentions, quietly flagging a delegate's veiled threat for her handler, Marek Voss. The chapter establishes her invisible craft and her pride in it. Emotional beat: controlled competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: A Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A man named Felix intercepts her after a late session, thanking her for saving his life in Sarajevo—an event she cannot recall. He leaves a card with only a time and place. She checks her records; nothing exists. Emotional beat: unease, the first crack in her ordered world.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Unable to resist, she meets Felix at a shuttered tram depot. He reveals he works off-book for a European security service and owes a debt: intercepted chatter suggesting an attack timed to the summit's closing ceremony, designed to read as infrastructure failure. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity tipping into obligation.

chapters.title: What Marek Knows
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She brings the intel to Marek, expecting action; instead he dismisses it too smoothly and warns her off 'ghost stories.' His deflection feels rehearsed. Emotional beat: betrayal's first cold taste.

chapters.title: The Interpreter's Ear
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix explains how he identified Xanthe: years ago, an anonymous voice on a compromised line rerouted him away from an ambush—a voiceprint match led to her. He doesn't know if she did it deliberately. Emotional beat: his own uncertainty about the woman he's recruiting.

chapters.title: Accident, Scheduled
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Together they decode the chatter: a gas main breach beneath the summit hall, timed to the closing vote. The target isn't the delegates—it's the treaty itself. Emotional beat: dread crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: Invisible No More
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Following the money trail through translation contracts, Xanthe realizes the operation is funded inside the delegation's logistics office—the people she's worked beside for years. Emotional beat: paranoia; every colleague becomes a suspect.

chapters.title: The Handler's Hand
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix digs into Marek's past and finds a pattern: three prior 'accidents' at failed talks, each one Marek had flagged then buried. They realize Marek may be the architect—or the fall guy. Emotional beat: vertigo of shifting loyalties.

chapters.title: Close Quarters
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Trapped together during a lockdown drill gone wrong, Xanthe and Felix evade a surveillance sweep and, adrenaline high, cross a personal line. Emotional beat: intimacy born of danger; love against duty takes root.

chapters.title: The Dead Drop
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A contact inside the logistics office agrees to pass them the attack timeline but is found dead hours later, staged as suicide. The message: they are being watched. Emotional beat: grief and guilt sharpening resolve.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Reviewing old recordings, Xanthe finds proof she did save Felix in Sarajevo—she rerouted him deliberately, then erased her own memory of it under pressure from Marek. Her invisibility was never natural; it was manufactured. Emotional beat: identity shattered and remade.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Lake
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She confronts Marek privately. He admits the earlier accidents were sanctioned 'pressure valves' to keep talks failing on schedule—and claims the coming attack exceeds even his orders. Someone above him is escalating. Emotional beat: horrified complicity; the enemy has a face and a hierarchy.

chapters.title: Turned
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Marek, cornered, offers Xanthe a deal: help him control the fallout and he'll give her the operational file. Felix distrusts him completely. Emotional beat: uneasy triangulation; duty and justice pull apart.

chapters.title: The File
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The handoff goes wrong—Marek's safehouse is raided by the conspirators' cleaners. Felix and Xanthe recover the file but must go fully dark, hiding in a derelict border station: their own improvised safehouse. Emotional beat: fugitive intimacy; no way back.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Deciphering the file, they learn the exact mechanism: a pressure valve rigged to the summit hall's heating system, set for the closing ceremony in two days. They also learn the escalation's author: Deputy Secretary Ilse Brandt. Emotional beat: clarity and terror in equal measure.

chapters.title: No One to Call
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Every official channel is compromised—Brandt controls the security detail. Their only option is to weaponize visibility: force the plot into the open where it can't look like an accident. Emotional beat: the leap from hiding to exposure.

chapters.title: Interpreting the Enemy
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Using her access as interpreter, Xanthe plants a mistranslation in Brandt's earpiece—a false confirmation that triggers the conspirators to move early. It's the riskiest thing she's ever done with language. Emotional beat: her invisible skill turned into a blade.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The team moves early; Felix infiltrates the plant room while Xanthe keeps Brandt occupied at a midnight reception. The device is found—but arming it remotely was a decoy; the real charge is elsewhere. Emotional beat: victory curdling into horror.

chapters.title: Closing Ceremony
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Summit day. From the interpreter's booth, Xanthe spots the real trigger—a delegate's briefcase transmitter—and must break every rule of her profession, speaking out of turn on an open channel to stall the vote. Emotional beat: courage at maximum cost.

chapters.title: What Accidents Look Like
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix reaches the briefcase as Brandt's cleaner activates it; a brutal struggle ends with the device disabled and Felix gravely wounded. Security, tipped by Xanthe's broadcast, swarms the hall. Brandt is arrested mid-ceremony. Emotional beat: climax—blood, noise, and the treaty signed anyway.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. In the aftermath, Xanthe testifies off the record to a tribunal, trading her anonymity for accountability. Marek faces charges; some names stay buried, an imperfect justice she accepts. Felix survives, changed. Emotional beat: reckoning; justice outside the law, paid for in full.

chapters.title: Felix and the Safehouse
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Months later, Xanthe and Felix share a quiet house outside Lyon—no longer hiding, just private. She takes one last interpreting job, openly this time. The favor that never happened has finally been repaid, both directions. Emotional beat: peace earned, identity chosen, love kept.
